title: Estate use cases
subtitle: What people and machinery actually do here, and which surface each act happens on
actor_note: Actors are the estate's own authorship enum (R38) — human, frontier, house — plus external for another node. The estate already records who caused every event in exactly these terms, so a use case naming a different cast of actors would be describing a different system.

actors.name: You (the owner)
actors.note: The only actor who may sign. Everything consequential terminates in a decision here.

actors.name: Benny (the agent)
actors.note: May propose and may never authorise (ADR-001). Reads, drafts, raises.

actors.name: The estate (deterministic machinery)
actors.note: Scheduled tasks, folds, sweeps and gates. Emits facts; exercises no judgement.

actors.name: Another node
actors.note: optimus, homeassistant, or a publisher we fetch from. Reachable, not trusted.

verification_note: `exercised` means this flow was run end to end against the live estate and its result observed. `declared` means it is taken from the surface's own registered description and has NOT been run. The difference is recorded because a use-case map that reads uniformly confident about both is the same lie as a gauge reporting zero from an empty population.

use_cases.name: Authorise a piece of work
use_cases.goal: Turn a proposal into an authorisation the rest of the estate can cite.
use_cases.trigger: Something is waiting in the signing queue.
preconditions: The governance ledger's hash chain verifies.
flow: Open the Gov arc. Each card shows why, what it rests on, what it costs and whether it reverses — before any button.
Read the evidence disclosure if the decision turns on it.
Sign, or decline with a reason.
use_cases.outcome: A proposal_signed event with authorship human and your identity from the session.
refuses: The client cannot choose the signer.
Signing onto a ledger whose chain does not verify is refused.

use_cases.name: Raise work for a decision
use_cases.goal: Put a finding forward without acting on it.
use_cases.trigger: The agent, or a script, finds work worth doing.
flow: POST /api/gov_raise with a proposalId, title, rationale and any derivedFrom subjects.
The proposal appears in the Gov queue and nothing else happens.
An identical re-raise writes nothing; a changed one refreshes in place.
use_cases.outcome: A proposal_raised event with authorship frontier, awaiting a human.
refuses: A proposal without a rationale is refused.
A settled proposal cannot be re-raised.
derivedFrom must be subject ids, never prose.
use_cases.gap: There is no screen for this. Raising is reachable only from a command line or an agent — see the sitemap's routes-with-no-panel.

use_cases.name: Prove where a thing came from
use_cases.goal: Answer 'who caused this, and on whose authority' for any subject in the estate.
use_cases.trigger: A reviewer asks, or something looks wrong.
preconditions: An estate store exists and its ledgers verify.
flow: Open the Lineage arc. Coverage is shown before the rows, on purpose.
Filter by kind and pick the subject.
Read its parents, its machines, and the authorship split.
use_cases.outcome: The subject's full recorded history, with what is NOT recorded stated plainly.
refuses: A subject from a failing ledger is shown but never counted as evidence.
Edges are declared, never inferred.
Ledger-to-world completeness reports NOT MEASURABLE without a sweep.

use_cases.name: Replay what happened, step by step
use_cases.goal: Walk an execution one event at a time and see what the system believed at each point.
use_cases.trigger: Understanding an outcome after the fact.
preconditions: The subject has more than one recorded event.
flow: Select the subject; the trail opens on the most recent event.
Prev / Next, or the arrow keys, walk the history.
The tick rail colours each event by who caused it.
use_cases.outcome: The event's own payload plus the projection the system would have returned then.
refuses: The projector is last-write-wins, so the field is called projection, not state — earlier facts are absent, never retracted.

use_cases.name: Onboard an application
use_cases.goal: Bring new software into the estate so it is authorised, stored once, placed everywhere and remembered.
use_cases.trigger: You want an application on one or more machines.
flow: propose — writes a proposal and stops. Nothing is fetched.
decide — you sign in the Gov arc. There is no way to skip this.
acquire — fetches once into the content-addressed store, citing the signature.
place — materialises a copy per machine, each recording the same cause.
remember — rebuild the manual so the agent knows the application exists.
use_cases.outcome: An installed application whose entire path is provable from the ledger.
refuses: acquire and place refuse while the proposal is open, declined or absent.
There is no --force.

use_cases.name: Download once, use everywhere
use_cases.goal: Stop paying for the same file twice across machines.
use_cases.trigger: A release, installer or model is needed on more than one node.
preconditions: The publisher gives a hash, or you accept fetching once to learn it.
flow: acquire with --expected-hash; if the blob is held the source is never opened.
place it on each machine that needs it.
ls shows what is held and where every copy lives.
evict retires a copy; the blob survives.
use_cases.outcome: One stored copy, many recorded placements, and a transfer-avoided figure that is real.
refuses: A --caused-by naming a proposal must name one a human actually signed.
Eviction never destroys the blob.

use_cases.name: Notice that a machine has gone quiet
use_cases.goal: Know which nodes and services are alive without assuming silence means health.
use_cases.trigger: The scheduled sweep, every five minutes; the collector, every fifteen.
preconditions: Each node writes its own chained log.
flow: Each node sweeps its own services and records only transitions.
The collector pulls the remote logs and folds one board.
A node that stopped reporting is carried as a blind spot.
use_cases.outcome: A board that distinguishes 'down' from 'not heard from'.
refuses: Chains are never concatenated.
A failed pull must not make a node vanish from the board.

use_cases.name: Hand a reviewer the evidence
use_cases.goal: Produce, from cold, a document that shows whether the estate is governed — including what cannot be shown.
use_cases.trigger: An audit, or your own periodic check.
preconditions: Ledgers exist; a sweep can reach the store.
flow: Run the sweep to reconcile disk against ledger.
Generate the pack; read the verdict before the table.
Check the 'Of' column: a count means nothing without its population.
use_cases.outcome: One document a reviewer can read without a tour of the codebase.
refuses: NOT MEASURABLE never masquerades as clean.
A gauge with an empty population is named as vacuous.
Exit 0 only when every defect is measured, zero and non-empty.

use_cases.name: Ask the estate a question about itself
use_cases.goal: Get an answer from the operating manual rather than from the model's general knowledge.
use_cases.trigger: You do not remember how something works.
preconditions: The manual has been built and loaded; an embedding model and a chat model are served.
flow: Build the manual from manual.json; the build fails rather than describe something absent.
Load it: graph triples for traversal, chunks for retrieval, a PageIndex tree for navigation.
Ask. Answers are graded for groundedness and labelled.
use_cases.outcome: An answer traceable to a section of the manual, or an honest 'I do not know'.
refuses: A partial load is reported as partial, never as success.
Ungrounded answers come back flagged, not silently.

use_cases.name: Recall what was done in a past session
use_cases.goal: Find the work, the reasoning and the artefacts of an earlier session.
use_cases.trigger: Picking up something started days or weeks ago.
preconditions: The memory graph has scanned the relevant agent activity.
flow: Configure where the memory graph scans (Memory Setup).
Search or browse sessions in Memory; the Lifelog gives the same span as a timeline of commits and agent actions.
Open one session in the Session Graph to walk its recursive inputs and outputs.
use_cases.outcome: The session, its lineage, and what it produced.

use_cases.name: See how the pipeline produced an output
use_cases.goal: Inspect the model calls, gate verdicts and retrievals behind a generated artefact.
use_cases.trigger: An output looks wrong, or needs defending.
flow: Open Benny Record and select the output.
Replay the production path: every model call, gate verdict and retrieval.
use_cases.outcome: The chain of steps that produced the artefact.

use_cases.name: Inspect a signed manifest
use_cases.goal: Read what a deterministic-zone manifest will do before it runs.
use_cases.trigger: Reviewing planned work an agent has drafted.
flow: Open Manifests and pick the registered manifest.
Read it as a DAG rather than as JSON.
use_cases.outcome: An understanding of the planned execution, before authorising it.

use_cases.name: Watch the whole mesh at once
use_cases.goal: See memory, documents, code, flows and runs in one place.
use_cases.trigger: Starting a session, or checking on long-running work.
flow: Open Mission Control for the ecosystem rollup, resources and capabilities.
Open Bridge for the cognitive mesh across memory, documents, code, flows and runs.
use_cases.outcome: Current state without opening five screens.

use_cases.name: Hold and edit the estate's own files
use_cases.goal: Browse and change app files without leaving the estate.
flow: Open Files, navigate to the file, edit it.

use_cases.name: Serve and test a local model
use_cases.goal: Run a model on this machine rather than sending work elsewhere.
preconditions: A model is present on disk.
flow: Open Local LLM.
Load a model and test it with WebGPU or Hugging Face.
use_cases.outcome: A model serving locally, which the rest of the estate can use.

use_cases.name: Undo a change to the estate's own configuration
use_cases.goal: Roll back settings, spaces or custom development changes.
flow: Open Time Travel and select what to undo.

use_cases.name: Manage the operator account
use_cases.goal: Keep the identity that signs things correct and secured.
flow: Open User and update your name or password.
use_cases.outcome: The identity the signing path reads from the session is current.
use_cases.note: This matters more than it looks: gov_sign takes the signer from the session, so this surface defines who the ledger will name.
